subject: Accounts
title: The Father of Accounting
text: In 1494, Luca Pacioli, an Italian friar and mathematician, published 'Summa de arithmetica' in Venice. It was the first printed work on the double-entry system – the same system you use in every journal entry today.

subject: Auditing
title: Why is it called 'Audit'?
text: The word 'audit' comes from the Latin 'audire' – to hear. In early days accounts were read out aloud and the auditor 'heard' them before approving.

subject: Law
title: 150+ years and still working
text: The Indian Contract Act was enacted on 25 April 1872 and came into force on 1 September 1872 with 266 sections. Every contract question you solve still rests on this 150-year-old law.

subject: Costing
title: Taylor + Gilbreths = Time & Motion Study
text: Time and motion study combines Frederick Taylor's time study with Frank and Lillian Gilbreth's motion study. The Gilbreth family later became famous through the book and film 'Cheaper by the Dozen'.

subject: Law
title: The smoke ball that made contract law
text: In Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co (1893), a company promised £100 to anyone who caught flu after using its smoke ball. Mrs Carlill did, sued and won – the court held the advert was a general offer to the whole world.
source: Wikipedia – Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co

subject: Financial Management
title: The Rule of 72 is 500+ years old
text: Divide 72 by the interest rate to estimate how many years money takes to double. An early reference to this rule appears in Luca Pacioli's Summa of 1494 – the same book that gave us double-entry!

subject: Income Tax
title: Why income tax came to India
text: India's first Income-tax Act was introduced in February 1860 by James Wilson, British India's first finance minister, to refill the treasury after the 1857 crisis. It received assent on 24 July 1860 and had 259 sections.

subject: Auditing
title: The scandal that ended a Big Five firm
text: After Enron's fraud became public in October 2001, its auditor Arthur Andersen – then one of the five largest audit firms in the world – collapsed. The USA passed the Sarbanes–Oxley Act in 2002 in response.

subject: GST
title: GST was born at midnight
text: GST was launched at a special midnight session (30 June – 1 July 2017) in the Central Hall of Parliament, through the 101st Constitutional Amendment. 1 July is marked as GST Day.

subject: Costing
title: Where the learning curve came from
text: In 1936, T. P. Wright, an aircraft engineer, found that every time total aircraft production doubled, the labour time needed per aircraft fell by about 20%. This is the learning curve you study in costing.

subject: Law
title: The minor who changed contract law
text: In Mohori Bibee v Dharmodas Ghose (1903), a minor mortgaged his property to a moneylender. The Privy Council held that an agreement with a minor is totally void – the rule you apply in exams today.
source: Wikipedia – Mohori Bibee v Dharmodas Ghose

subject: Strategic Management
title: Five forces, one article
text: Michael Porter's Five Forces framework was first published in Harvard Business Review in 1979. Over four decades later it is still the starting point for industry analysis.

subject: Accounts
title: Debit and Credit – the Latin roots
text: It is said that Pacioli's Summa used the Latin words 'debere' (to owe) and 'credere' (to entrust) for the two sides of a transaction – the roots of our words Debit and Credit.

subject: Financial Management
title: A Nobel Prize for capital structure
text: The Modigliani–Miller theorem on capital structure was first proposed in 1958. Franco Modigliani received the 1985 Nobel Prize in Economics for this and other work.

subject: Income Tax
title: A new Income-tax Act from 2026
text: The Income-tax Act, 2025 came into force on 1 April 2026, replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961 after more than six decades of amendments.

subject: Strategic Management
title: Kodak invented the digital camera
text: Steven Sasson built the first self-contained digital camera at Kodak in 1975. It weighed about 3.6 kg and had just 100 × 100 pixels (0.01 megapixel). A classic strategy lesson: inventing a technology is not the same as building your strategy around it.

subject: GST
title: GST's ancestor – VAT
text: The value-added tax was devised by Maurice Lauré of the French tax authority. It was first tried in 1954 in France's Ivory Coast colony, and France introduced it at home in 1958. GST belongs to this VAT family.

subject: Auditing
title: India's biggest wake-up call for auditors
text: In 2009, Satyam's chairman B. Ramalinga Raju confessed that the company's accounts had been manipulated by about ₹7,000 crore. The scandal shaped many audit reforms that followed.

subject: Accounts
title: 1 July – a double celebration
text: ICAI was established on 1 July 1949 under the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949. GST was also launched on 1 July (2017) – so 1 July is both CA Day and GST Day.
source: Wikipedia – ICAI; Goods and Services Tax (India)

subject: Financial Management
title: Don't put all your eggs in one basket
text: Harry Markowitz published his portfolio theory in 1952, showing how diversification reduces risk. He received the 1990 Nobel Prize in Economics for it.

subject: Costing
title: The Gantt chart is over 100 years old
text: Henry Gantt created the Gantt chart in the 1910s. It was later used to plan huge projects such as the Hoover Dam.

subject: Strategic Management
title: Kaplan – from costing to scorecards
text: Robin Cooper and Robert Kaplan brought Activity-Based Costing into the spotlight in the 1980s. Kaplan, with David Norton, then gave the world the Balanced Scorecard in a 1992 article.

subject: Strategic Management
title: Stars, cash cows and dogs
text: The BCG growth-share matrix was introduced in 1970 in the Boston Consulting Group essay 'The Product Portfolio'.
